title: Italian community asks why man died in custody in Quebec
article: As Claudio Castagnetta's body arrived in his hometown of Palermo, Italy, Quebec City's Italian community organized a peaceful candlelight vigil last night, desperately seeking the truth about his sudden death while in police custody.

"Does this look like a criminal to you?" cried out Alessandro Porcaro, barely containing his anger as he pointed to a poster of Mr. Castagnetta while others among the small group of about 50 people urged him to remain calm.

Mr. Castagnetta, 32, was arrested on Sept. 18 after he entered a store barefoot and appeared confused and disoriented. It took at least six police officers using physical force and a stun gun to subdue Mr. Castagnetta. Two days later, Mr. Castagnetta, who had no criminal record or known psychological disorder, died from self-inflicted wounds after reportedly banging his head on a wall while still in custody.

The tragic death has left many Quebec City residents bewildered, raising numerous questions as to why Mr. Castegnetta was detained in jail for two days on a charge of disorderly conduct and resisting arrest instead of receiving proper medical attention. Unconfirmed reports stated that a hockey helmet was placed on his head to protect him during his incarceration.

"It is a shame that at 32 years of age someone would die simply because he walked barefoot and because he behaved in an abnormal way," said one of Mr. Castagnetta's friends, who asked not to be named.
"It is a shame that he died because of \[a\] sudden moment of distress."

Mr. Castegnetta arrived in Canada five years ago and recently obtained his Canadian citizenship. He was working as a translator while completing a master's degree in business administration at Laval University.
